blocking.section: Runbooks > Holding deliveries during recovery (step 2); Runbooks > Region loss (non-home, step 4)
blocking.issue: Hold step 2 tells the operator to set `requireApproval: true` on every Environment. The Configuration model allows that only when `promotion.from` is also set, and the root Environment of a promotion chain has no `from`. RA-2's `staging` is one example. An operator following step 2 commits an `environments.yaml` that fails validation, or cannot gate the root Environment at all. Region-loss step 4 has the same problem. If the lost Region holds a root-Environment Cluster, "first commit `requireApproval: true`" is not possible, so only a merge freeze holds it. The hold does still work for the root Environment, because the recovery ref pins what it renders, but the document never says so. The reader is left with an instruction that cannot be carried out.
blocking.evidence: HA doc, hold step 2: "Push a recovery ref at that commit, plus a commit setting `requireApproval: true` on every Environment in `control/environments.yaml` (no digest changes)". Region loss step 4: "approve nothing under `requireApproval`, else freeze merges to the tracked branch or first commit `requireApproval: true`, a tightening that needs no approval." Configuration model, Environment: "from: staging # required when promotion is set" and "Every `Environment.spec` field is optional ... `promotion.from` chains MUST be acyclic (RZ-CFG-022)." Deployment topologies, RA-2: "`staging` and `prod`, one Cluster each; `prod` `Environment.spec.promotion`: `from: staging`, `requireApproval`".
blocking.fix: In hold step 2, replace "on every Environment" with "on every Environment with `promotion.from`; a root Environment cannot be gated, so the recovery ref alone pins what it renders". In Region-loss step 4, replace "else freeze merges to the tracked branch or first commit `requireApproval: true`" with "else commit `requireApproval: true` where `promotion.from` exists, and freeze merges while the lost Region holds a root-Environment Cluster". Keep the change word-neutral, because the body is at 4,493 of 4,500 words.

blocking.section: Game days GD-10 (and GD-9 via "as GD-10"); Runbooks > Holding deliveries during recovery
blocking.issue: GD-10's pass criteria contradict the document's own prediction for a rebuild. The hold section says that after a rebuild no Node is qualified, so the published Node count can collapse. Derived ceilings then go to the full limit, and hot-key GCRA calls open shard breakers. GD-10 requires that the count drop at most 10% and that no State client breaker opens. A team running GD-10 under the current design, with OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 undecided, fails a drill that gates M2. The document offers no way to pass it.
blocking.evidence: Hold section: "After a rebuild, or a restore without a revocation list, no Node is qualified, so the first `HeartbeatReply` can collapse the published count until OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 decides" and "Hot-key GCRA 2 × requests → up to N_serving × 2 × requests per window, opening shard breakers". GD-10: "Every promoted digest equals its Nodes' active digest before reconnect; the published count drops at most 10% (target); no State client breaker opens". Scalability CE-7 and CE-10 use the 10% criterion only for restarts and failovers where qualification survives in committed state.
blocking.fix: Change GD-10's pass criteria to: "Every promoted digest equals its Nodes' active digest before reconnect; limits with declared ceilings stay within their fail-open row; the count criterion of CE-10 applies once OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 decides (a)". Or run GD-10 with declared per-Node ceilings on every `limits[]` entry and drop "the published count drops at most 10%" until OQ-9 decides. Mark OQ-9 as blocking for GD-10 as well.

non_blocking.suggestion: `λ_storm`, `c_hs` and `C2` are not defined in this document, although the new symbol legend fixed the others. Capacity planning's check is λ_storm × (c_hs + c_up) ≤ 10% of survivor CPU, so this document also leaves out `c_up`. Define them in the legend ("λ_storm the reconnect handshake rate, c_hs and c_up the CPU per TLS handshake and per upgrade GCRA call, per Capacity planning"; "C2 the handshake benchmark of Performance budgets"), or use the full Capacity planning expression.

"A running Rollout into the lost Cluster lags, then ends `rolled-back` or `paused`": with `autoRollback: true`, a revert cannot reach lost Nodes that had already activated the new Revision. Once they exceed the lagging threshold, the Rollout ends `failed` and pages an operator (Control plane and GitOps). Add `failed` so on-call staff expect the page.

Step 1 runs non-home step 5, which uses `ruralz rollout status` and a revert against Ruralz Control. Neither can run until the restore, and while Ruralz Control is lost no empty-plan Rollouts can happen. Say that non-home step 5 is replaced by the hold (step 6) in this case, or limit step 1 to non-home steps 1 to 3.
